claims.text: The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi thin films or nanoribbons have a high density of deposition-induced defects and strain.
Post-deposition annealing reduces defect concentrations in the FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons.
Post-deposition annealing improves crystallographic ordering in the FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons.
Reduced defect density and modified grain boundaries promote a more homogeneous magnetic-domain structure.
Increased microstructural order produces a more uniform magnetic phase transition.
Increased microstructural order makes the magnetic phase transition more reversible.
Annealing promotes controlled nucleation and growth of magnetic domains under applied fields.
The proposed changes in magnetic-domain behavior enhance the magnetocaloric effect.
The proposed increase in transition reversibility reduces hysteretic energy losses.
Annealed samples will exhibit a greater reversible entropy change than as-deposited samples.
Annealed samples will exhibit narrower magnetic hysteresis loops than as-deposited samples.
The proposed operating regime uses applied magnetic fields below approximately 0.5 T.
The proposed operating regime uses cycle frequencies below approximately 10 Hz because cycle frequency is limited by heat-transfer rate.
The proposed nanoscale samples generally have thicknesses below 100 nm.
Overextended annealing may cause excessive grain growth and place the material outside the effective regime.
The magnitudes of entropy-change enhancement and hysteresis reduction depend on annealing parameters and the extent of defect reduction.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant increase in reversible entropy change and a reduction in hysteresis-loop area relative to the as-deposited control would falsify the hypothesis.
